title: Motion for an Extension of Time

pages.text:
U.S. Department of Justice
Office of the Solicitor General
The Solicitor General
 Washington, D.C. 20530
November 6, 2026
Honorable Scott S. Harris
Clerk
Supreme Court of the United States
Washington, D.C. 20543
Corey Duran Berry v. United States,
No. 25-7026
Dear Mr. Harris:
On October 13, 2026, the Court granted the petition for a writ of certiorari in the above-
captioned case.  Petitioner’s brief is currently due on November 27, 2026.
Because of scheduling difficulties and the press of other matters before the Court, the
parties respectfully request, under Rule 30.4 of the Rules of this Court, a seven-day extension of
time, to and including December 4, 2026, within which to file the petitioner’s brief; and an eight-
day extension of time, to and including January 12, 2027, within which to file the government’s
brief as respondent.  If those extensions are granted, the reply brief would be due on February 11,
2027, which would permit oral argument during the Court’s February 2027 argument session.
The parties have agreed on the schedule above, which accommodates the litigation
schedules of counsel.
Sincerely,
D. John Sauer
Solicitor General
